The Market for Saved Funds

In micro, the question was whether one person saves. In macro, the stage is a market where the whole country pools its saving.

The interest rate is the price of borrowed money. A higher rate coaxes out more saving. It also scares off borrowers who wanted to invest. Where the two meet, as the formulas below show, sits the equilibrium rate. A government deficit eats into the pool, pushes the rate up, and crowds private investment out.

For example, imagine all your classmates pool their 🐷 piggy-bank 💰 money in one box. If many friends want to borrow and money is scarce, the charge goes up. If the teacher borrows big first, less is left for everyone else.

S(r)=S0+srS(r) = S_0 + s rS(r)=S0​+sr
I(r)=I0−brI(r) = I_0 - b rI(r)=I0​−br
r∗=I0−S0+Ds+br^* = \frac{I_0 - S_0 + D}{s + b}r∗=s+bI0​−S0​+D​

Examples & Exercises

The government runs a deficit D=20D = 20D=20 while base saving stays at S0=40S_0 = 40S0​=40.

What happens to the interest rate and to private investment?

Show proof

  1. With no deficit, equilibrium is r∗=(I0−S0)/(s+b)=(100−40)/(4+6)=6r^* = (I_0 - S_0) / (s + b) = (100 - 40) / (4 + 6) = 6r∗=(I0​−S0​)/(s+b)=(100−40)/(4+6)=6 and investment is I=100−6⋅6=64I = 100 - 6 \cdot 6 = 64I=100−6⋅6=64. The deficit 202020 shifts total saving left by that much, so r∗=(100−40+20)/10=8r^* = (100 - 40 + 20) / 10 = 8r∗=(100−40+20)/10=8.

  2. At the new rate, investment is I=100−6⋅8=52I = 100 - 6 \cdot 8 = 52I=100−6⋅8=52. The crowded-out amount is given by the formula below — not the whole deficit, only 121212.

    The higher rate coaxes household saving from 646464 up to 727272, covering the other 888.

    Even so, saving = investment shrinks from 646464 to 525252.

    ΔI=−bD/(s+b)=−6⋅20/10=−12\Delta I = -b D / (s + b) = -6 \cdot 20 / 10 = -12ΔI=−bD/(s+b)=−6⋅20/10=−12

Households tighten their belts and base saving rises from S0=40S_0 = 40S0​=40 to 606060 (there is no deficit).

What happens to the interest rate and investment?

Show proof

  1. The saving curve shifts right, so equilibrium is r∗=(100−60)/(4+6)=4r^* = (100 - 60) / (4 + 6) = 4r∗=(100−60)/(4+6)=4 — down 222 points from the old 666. When loanable money is plentiful, its price, the interest rate, falls.

  2. Investment becomes I=100−6⋅4=76I = 100 - 6 \cdot 4 = 76I=100−6⋅4=76, up 121212 from the old 646464. In this market, extra saving turns into exactly extra investment — the rise in saving, 76−64=1276 - 64 = 1276−64=12, matches to the last unit.
